public_rationale: The claim says AI agents will not work well until major progress is made in common sense. It gives no deadline. The contract settles the claim early only in two cases. It is contradicted if agents are shown to reliably complete realistic multi-step tasks while no major commonsense advance is documented. It is supported if a documented commonsense breakthrough is what made agents work well. No dated evidence shows either event. In the paper's September 2025 revision, the best agent on TheAgentCompany completed 30% of tasks autonomously (e1). In July 2025, OpenAI said its ChatGPT agent was still in its early stages and could still make mistakes (e2). Neither item shows agents working reliably, and neither says whether any commonsense progress happened. With no deadline, continued shortfalls do not settle the forecast. The hedged part, that progress 'may require wholesale revisions' in how AI is approached, cannot be tested on its own.
limitations: There is no agreed measure of 'working well' for agents and no agreed marker of 'major progress in common sense'.
The evidence covers one benchmark and one vendor statement. It does not cover agent deployment more broadly.
Neither evidence item looks at commonsense reasoning, so the record says nothing about the claim's condition.
